newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey puts out fire at unused Iraqi oil pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Turkey puts out fire at unused Iraqi oil pipeline.

text.p: Turkish fire brigades on Friday put out a fire caused by a rebel Kurdish bomb attack on an unused Iraqi oil pipeline in the southeast, oil officials said.
Lost throughput could be about 30,000 barrels, they said.
The fire, caused by the bomb explosion on Wednesday night, was extinguished in the morning by local fire brigades and state oil company Botas, which operates the pipeline.
"The fire inside the pipeline has been put out," an official from Botas told Reuters. "But the oil that has leaked is still burning but that is not so important for us."

Militants of the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) planted explosives on the larger, unused pipeline of the the 986-km (616-mile) twin lines from Kirkuk oilfields to the Ceyhan terminal on the Mediterranean.

Officials said Iraq's oil sales under a United Nations plan through the thinner, 40-inch pipeline was not disrupted and a tanker sailed to Bulgaria on Wednesday after it was loaded 135,179 tonnes of crude.
The explosion occurred on the 46-inch line at the PSE-4 pumping station near Sogutlu village in Mardin province, near the Iraqi border.
Provincial officials in Mardin said the fire had spread along the unused pipeline to the nearby town of Omerli.
Mardin governor Fikret Guven said they would boost security along the pipeline by building an asphalt road to provide easier access and by more frequent inspections along the line.
The pipeline has so far been attacked three times in the southeast by the PKK, but Guven said the latest attack was the most serious.
